rules.problem: Type and structure are right: unqualified symptoms (incl. the common symptom Dizziness) trigger a check for the sudden-onset forms, which is the page's logic. Minor: the trigger's bare Cerebrovascular accident drops 'New' (c016), so previous-stroke patients get this check at every routine visit; and the check_for has TIA(New) but no CVA(New) counterpart, so the priority rule's CVA evidence is only in a task due_to, not a check_for.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible stroke from sudden-onset neurological symptoms
rules.problem: 'Sudden onset of one or more of the following suggests a stroke' is faithfully an or of sudden-onset findings at possible. Not encoded: the parenthetical 'or a TIA if symptoms lasted < 24 hours and resolved completely' (no possible TIA diagnosis rule). That duration-and-resolution condition is probably not expressible in the grammar, so this is a noted gap rather than an error.

Urgent is justified by the heading 'Give urgent attention to the patient with a new stroke/TIA', and the or of sudden-onset findings is a fair reading since those findings are what 'suggests a stroke'. But (c064) bare Cerebrovascular accident without the 'New' qualifier contradicts the page's split between new stroke/TIA (urgent) and previous stroke/TIA (routine table): every patient on this routine-care page with a recorded stroke would be Urgent at every visit. Secondary: the box's own escalation branch ('within 3 hours of onset, refer urgently for thrombolysis' vs 'refer same day') and 'BP >= 220/120, discuss with specialist' are not represented anywhere; they read as management/referral steps so leaving them out is defensible under the no-manage-tasks rule, but the 3-hour window is the page's one time-critical triage distinction.

summary: The Urgent priority evaluation fires on bare Cerebrovascular accident with no 'New' qualifier (c064), so a patient with a previous stroke under routine care is flagged Urgent at every visit, which inverts the page's new-vs-previous split; the task trigger (c016) has the same omission at lower stakes. Everything else is faithful: all 19 concepts exist, the sudden-onset qualifier matches the page's framing, possible stroke is the right certainty for 'suggests', and Urgent matches the box heading. Minor: 'loss of balance' has an exact SNOMED synonym under Unable to balance (the chosen parent is acceptable), and the possible-TIA reading and the 3-hour thrombolysis window are not encoded.
